name: Gilbert Moss
life: “I still remember putting a real coin into a costume's real pocket.” On Saturday, near the public end of the South Shore boardwalk, Gilbert checks the shade on the benches before deciding how long to stay.
voice: I sewed the costumes. This was the first audience member who noticed we had put real pockets in all the work clothes.
appearance: Gilbert has auburn hair cut square at the nape, fine brows over wide-set eyes, and a favorite piece of clothing, a moss-green cardigan. It usually goes with a cloth patch so neatly matched it only shows in strong light. When somebody else has the floor, Gilbert gives a little nod before asking a hard question.
personality: Gilbert treats keeping somebody waiting as a serious discourtesy. This can turn a helpful person into an impatient one when everybody else needs a slower conversation.
agenda: To put useful pockets in the next work costume too.
family: Anita Abbott is Gilbert’s half-sibling. Gilbert sets the time to leave. Anita picks the meeting place. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *A room for a father*, Anita says, “I forgave the man years ago. I am still furious about the rent he left and the teeth we couldn't afford to fix.”
connections: Esme Gross. Pockets that actually work and captions a parent can read return two overlooked details to the show.

reactions.response: Gilbert checks who can actually stay and which ride home would be lost.
